limits: For white wine, the main grapes together: 60 to 84%
For white wine, the complementary grapes together: 16 to 40%
For red and rosé wine, Pinot Noir: 60 to 84%
For red and rosé wine, Gamay: 16 to 40%
For red and rosé wine, the minor grapes together: at most 5%
rules.yield_base: 60 hl/ha for white, 55 for red and rosé

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Sauvignon Blanc and Pinot Noir sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.

blurb.text: A Loire Valley appellation for dry white, light red and rosé wines. Whites are 60% to 80% Sauvignon Blanc, blended with other grapes. It spreads over 1,300 acres in 24 communes of Loir-et-Cher and became an AOC in 1993.
